html:
Great Moravia was a Slavic state centred on the Morava River in today's Czech Republic and Slovakia, formed around 833 when Prince Mojmír I united Moravia with the lands of Nitra.

At its height under Svatopluk I in the 880s it ruled Bohemia, much of Slovakia and parts of Hungary and Poland. In 863 Prince Rastislav invited the Byzantine missionaries Cyril and Methodius, who created the Glagolitic script and taught in the Slavic language. Its strongholds at Mikulčice and Staré Město had stone churches and rich graves. After Svatopluk's death in 894 it was torn by family quarrels and fell to the Magyars soon after 900. Bohemia went its own way under the Přemyslids. See also the polity page Great Moravia.
sum: Great Moravia was a Slavic state centred on the Morava River in today's Czech Republic and Slovakia, formed around 833 when Prince Mojmír I united Moravia with the lands of Nitra.
